title: Go Core Path: Associate to Lead (140 Katas)
description: Structured Go learning from first programming principles to lead-level engineering, with guided pathways, testing discipline, bug-fix practice, and professional I/O patterns.

categories.title: Programming Essentials
categories.description: Zero-to-code foundations for learners new to programming and Go.
categories.learning_goal: Understand functions, conditionals, loops, and boundaries so you can turn plain rules into working code.

categories.title: Data and Logic
categories.description: Practical beginner problems using slices, maps, structs, and search/filter logic.
categories.learning_goal: Build confidence with common data operations and predictable return contracts.

categories.title: Well-Known Packages
categories.description: Focused katas for core standard library packages used in everyday Go code.
categories.learning_goal: Use common packages with confidence by implementing deterministic behavior contracts.

categories.title: Go Foundations
categories.description: Core syntax, control flow, and deterministic behavior with everyday coding patterns.
categories.learning_goal: Convert plain-language requirements into clear, testable Go functions that handle edge cases intentionally.

categories.title: Core Collections and Algorithms
categories.description: Slices, maps, generics, and algorithmic thinking for correctness under constraints.
categories.learning_goal: Use Go data structures and iteration patterns to solve problems without sacrificing readability or safety.

categories.title: Text, Data, and Transformations
categories.description: Parsing, formatting, and data transformation across structured and unstructured inputs.
categories.learning_goal: Design robust input/output behavior that is explicit about malformed data and contract guarantees.

categories.title: File, Time, and Config
categories.description: File handling, time-based behavior, and configuration safety in local systems.
categories.learning_goal: Handle operating-system boundaries and time-sensitive logic with predictable, testable behavior.

categories.title: Services and Boundaries
categories.description: HTTP, networking, and service composition across unstable external boundaries.
categories.learning_goal: Treat I/O boundaries as contracts and return safe behavior under failure and partial success.

categories.title: Service Patterns
categories.description: Reusable patterns for routing, middleware, storage, messaging, and observability.
categories.learning_goal: Compose service building blocks into maintainable, testable application layers.

categories.title: Concurrency and Reliability
categories.description: Lifecycle ownership, cancellation, coordination primitives, and resilient runtime behavior.
categories.learning_goal: Build concurrent systems that stay correct under load, interruption, and timing variance.

categories.title: Advanced Data Structures and Algorithms
categories.description: Thread-safe collections, probabilistic structures, graph algorithms, and engineering debugging.
categories.learning_goal: Implement and reason about advanced data structures with correctness proofs and performance awareness.

categories.title: Tooling and Security
categories.description: Validation, security primitives, testing practices, and production hardening.
categories.learning_goal: Apply security-first thinking and testing rigor to production Go code.

categories.title: CLI Tooling
categories.description: Build Unix-style command-line tools using Go's I/O and flag packages.
categories.learning_goal: Design composable CLI tools that handle stdin/stdout, flags, and error reporting correctly.

categories.title: Testing and Performance
categories.description: Advanced testing patterns, generics, reflection, and architectural design.
categories.learning_goal: Master Go's testing package and type system for professional-grade code.

categories.title: Bug Fix Lab
categories.description: Deliberately buggy implementations where learners diagnose failures and repair behavior without rewriting.
categories.learning_goal: Develop production debugging habits: reproduce, isolate, patch minimally, and confirm with regression tests.

categories.title: Databases and I/O
categories.description: Persistence, streaming, filesystem, and query-boundary contracts.
categories.learning_goal: Build confidence with database and I/O boundaries where correctness, error handling, and resource ownership are critical.
